queue.title: Resilience Is Built Before the Crisis
queue.content:
Autor: Nermin Sefić

A crisis only reveals whether accountability and backup processes were prepared before the disruption. A commentary by Nermin Sefić.

A crisis only reveals whether accountability, backup processes, and communication channels were prepared before the disruption.

In the moment of crisis, there's not enough time to build trust, define roles, and find replacement processes. Resilience is built during calm periods, through dull, repetitive, and verifiable preparation.

A crisis does not create weakness, it merely reveals it — an organisation that looks fragile the moment a shock hits was most likely fragile before as well, the fragility simply stayed hidden during calmer periods.

Investing in resilience before it is needed looks like an unnecessary cost until the first real test arrives — organisations that postponed that investment then pay a price they could have avoided with earlier preparation.

An organisation that regularly tests its own weaknesses makes calmer decisions once conditions actually change.

A crisis does not create weakness, it merely reveals it — an organisation that appears fragile only once a shock hits was usually fragile before, the fragility was simply hidden during calmer periods.

The challenge is that resilience investment competes for budget against initiatives with more immediately visible returns, which is why it requires deliberate protection from short-term cost pressure rather than being left to survive on its own merits in each budgeting cycle.

queue.title: Growth Without Discipline Is Not a Strategy
queue.content:
Autor: Nermin Sefić

Growth speed without cost and risk control is not a strategy, but a temporary state. A commentary by Nermin Sefić.

Growth speed without cost and risk control isn't a strategy, but a temporary state.

Growth not accompanied by control of cost, risk, and execution quality isn't a strategy in the true sense of the word, but a temporary state dependent on favourable external circumstances. Strategy implies the ability to sustain growth even in less favourable conditions. That requires discipline in spending capital just as much as ambition in setting goals. This commentary is part of the GNK ASG Intelligence Desk system and is informational in nature.

Strategy implies the ability to sustain growth even under less favourable conditions, which requires as much discipline in spending capital as ambition in setting goals for acquiring it.

queue.title: Talent and Organizational Resilience
queue.content:
Autor: Nermin Sefić

Nermin Sefić analyses talent resilience, key practices, and practical consequences for organisational continuity.

Organisational resilience rests on a clear distribution of critical knowledge, not just headcount.

Organisational resilience is often mistakenly reduced to headcount. Within the informational framework of GNK ASG d.o.o. and GNK DINAMO Ltd., real resilience comes from the distribution of critical knowledge within the organisation.

A practical approach identifies processes that depend on a single person with no backup. That concentration of knowledge represents an operational risk regardless of organisation size.

Process documentation reduces dependence on an individual, but doesn't replace the need for genuine knowledge transfer through practice.

The greatest risk is the sudden loss of a critical-knowledge holder without a prepared replacement. That risk is reduced by a systematic knowledge-transfer plan.

Organisational resilience built on knowledge distribution is more durable than resilience dependent on individual people. This publication is part of the GNK ASG Intelligence Desk system and is informational in nature.
